A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VG LLM research and contain readable main text, references, and Appendices A–D. Textual comparison and visual inspection support matching the equations, tables, and figures across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original VG LLM experiments on 3D scene understanding, spatial reasoning, and general multimodal benchmarks, including ablations and detailed appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and reports revised scene-understanding and ablation outcomes in the main text and appendix.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the Qwen2.5-VL-3B backbone, VGGT geometry encoder, two-layer MLP and additive feature fusion, text-generation objective, and task formulations. The revised frame counts are experimental settings, not architectural changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ScanRefer, Scan2Cap, and EmbodiedScan-based detection tasks, SPAR-7M and LLaVA-Hound training data, and spatial-reasoning and general multimodal benchmarks. Frame-count revisions remain within existing coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding tables, including SPAR for grounding, LEO and other captioning comparators, Qwen2.5-VL-3B for detection, and the explicit spatial-signal variants in Table 8. Several comparator scores change, but no comparison method is added or removed.

E3.justification: Appendix B changes uniform per-scene sampling from 24 to 32 frames for ScanRefer and from 16 to 32 for Scan2Cap. Other stated splits, training schedules, and testing procedures remain unchanged. Tables 3 and 8 relabel AP/AR as P/R, but Appendix A.2 retains the same count-based detection evaluation description, so a changed metric computation is not established.

E4.justification: Table 8 revises the evidence addressing whether latent geometry or predicted camera, depth, and point information helps scene understanding. The existing four-versus-six-frame robustness comparison also receives revised results. Ablation factors, spatial-reasoning ablations in Table 9, and appendix case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The revised scores do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Results are substantially replaced across Tables 1–3 and 8 and Appendix C. Refined ScanRefer Acc@0.25/0.5 changes from 51.0/45.1 to 53.5/47.5, and Scan2Cap CIDEr from 74.1 to 78.6; these accompany changed frame settings. Four-frame detection F1 for Qwen/VG LLM changes from 23.6/29.3 to 30.0/38.2, and six-frame F1 from 20.5/28.8 to 25.7/36.4. Category outcomes and ablation findings also change, including six-frame bathtub performance changing from an advantage to a deficit. Tables 4–7 and 9 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical representations and feature-fusion equations in Section 3 are unchanged. Neither version adds or revises formal assumptions, theoretical results, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: The central claims remain that latent geometry from video improves a 4B MLLM's scene understanding and spatial reasoning without explicit dense 3D inputs, including surpassing Gemini-1.5-Pro on VSI-Bench. The introduction substitutes precision-based detection margins for recall-based margins as supporting evidence; the abstract, contribution scope, and conclusion are unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 replaces the broad interpretation that additional spatial signals help with a more qualified conclusion: camera or depth information offers no clear benefit, while point maps help especially with dense captioning. The discussion of noisy explicit predictions is correspondingly narrowed to point maps. Appendix limitations concerning small objects, orientation, and depth estimation are unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 changes reported scene-understanding training time from 8 to 10 hours on the same eight H100 80G GPUs. Appendix B revises frame-preparation counts. Other implementation details, prompts, hardware, and code/data access information are retained.

R1.justification: The same 66 references and related-work positioning are retained. Adding Anthropic as the author of reference 1 is a bibliographic correction, not a newly cited work or changed research relationship.

P1.justification: Localized prose edits update the introduction's detection example, experimental summaries, ablation interpretation, and appendix settings. The title, abstract, method exposition, section order, and overall narrative structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Tables 3 and 8 change their detection headers from AP/AR to P/R, with small spacing and text-flow adjustments. The figure and table inventory and overall layout are retained; all qualitative figure content is unchanged. Numerical replacements are assessed under E6.

improvement.justification: The revised Table 8 discussion provides a more qualified account of which explicit spatial cues help, and the P/R headers better align with the count-based evaluation description in Appendix A.2. These are limited gains in interpretation and clarity. Higher reported scores alone do not establish improved quality: frame budgets change, and the PDFs do not explain the provenance of all revised detection values.
